types.name: Reciprocal trigonometric ratios and their identities

unknowns.asked: the exact value of sec, cosec or cot at a standard angle
two other ratios, from one of sec, cosec and cot and the quadrant
the solutions of a quadratic in sec or cosec written with tan squared or cot squared
the solutions of an equation in sec squared and tan, to three significant figures

constraints: angles are multiples of 30 or 45 degrees that are not on an axis
a root with |sec x| < 1 or |cosec x| < 1 gives no solution

misconceptions.text: Giving the ratio itself instead of its reciprocal
Replacing tan squared by sec squared and losing the 1
Taking the positive root without looking at the quadrant

unknowns.asked: the exact value of arcsin, arccos or arctan
the exact value of a trigonometric function of an inverse function, and of an inverse function of a trigonometric function
the largest domain and the greatest value of a function built from arcsin or arccos

misconceptions.text: Giving an angle with the right ratio that is outside the principal range

unknowns.asked: the single ratio equal to an expanded compound angle expression
sin(A + B) and cos(A - B) from given ratios of A and B
the exact value of a ratio of 15, 75, 105 or 165 degrees
tan of the double angle and of the angle plus a quarter of pi
tan(A + B), the exact angle A + B and tan 2A
tan x and the solutions of an equation with a compound angle

misconceptions.text: Using the same sign in the expansion of cos(A + B) as in the angle
Writing sin(A + B) as sin A + sin B

types.name: Symmetry relations of the trigonometric functions

unknowns.asked: the ratio of theta equal to a ratio of pi - theta, pi + theta, -theta, pi/2 - theta, pi/2 + theta or 2 pi - theta
four related values from the sine and cosine of an angle
the simplified form of a sum of two related ratios and its exact value

misconceptions.text: Changing the function when the relation keeps it, or keeping it when the relation changes it

types.name: Vectors: displacement, magnitude and parallel vectors

unknowns.asked: the displacement vector between two points
the magnitude of a vector
a distance, a unit vector and a point from a vector relation
the unknown components of two parallel vectors
the scalar multiple, the unknown coordinates and a distance for three collinear points
a side, a median and a parallelogram's diagonal from position vectors

constraints: exact questions use vectors with whole-number length
points are not collinear unless the question says so

misconceptions.text: Subtracting in the wrong order: a - b for the vector from A to B
Adding position vectors to get a displacement
Dividing by the square of the magnitude for a unit vector

types.name: The scalar product and the angle between vectors

unknowns.asked: the scalar product of two vectors
the constant that makes two vectors perpendicular
the angle between two vectors, in degrees
a scalar product, an exact angle of a triangle and a perpendicularity constant
scalar products of combinations of two vectors from their magnitudes and angle

misconceptions.text: Losing the sign of the scalar product and giving the acute angle
Expanding |a + b| squared as |a| squared plus |b| squared

unknowns.asked: the parameter of a given point on a line
the equation of the line through two points and an unknown coordinate of a third point on it
the vector equation of a line given in Cartesian form and where it crosses a coordinate plane
the acute angle between two lines
the speed of an object with constant velocity and when it is due north of a point
the closest point of a line to a given point and the shortest distance
a speed, the distance apart at a given time and the closest approach of two moving objects

misconceptions.text: Using a position vector as the direction of a line
Reversing the signs of the point when reading a Cartesian equation
Giving the obtuse angle between two lines

types.name: Pairs of lines: intersecting, parallel, coincident and skew

unknowns.asked: the parameters and the coordinates of the point where two lines meet
whether two parallel lines are distinct or the same line
whether two lines that are not parallel intersect or are skew
a common perpendicular direction and the shortest distance between two skew lines

constraints: the first two component equations always have one solution

misconceptions.text: Using the same parameter for both lines
Calling lines skew when they are parallel
